articles.title: 'That is my fault': Suchitra Mohanlal explains why Pranav Mohanlal, Vismaya Mohanlal are not fluent in Malayalam
articles.summary: Suchitra Mohanlal has opened up about Pranav Mohanlal's and Vismaya Mohanlal's familiarity with Malayalam. She also discussed the reasons Vismaya Moha.
articles.body: Suchitra Mohanlal has opened up about Pranav Mohanlal's and Vismaya Mohanlal's familiarity with Malayalam. She also discussed the reasons Vismaya Mohanlal takes time before committing to acting projects.According to Suchitra Mohanlal, both her children spent their school years in boarding schools. Their surroundings also meant they regularly communicated in English. She said this affected their connection with Malayalam as they grew older.In the interview with Can Media, Suchitra Mohanlal also accepted some responsibility for the situation. She revealed, âVismaya is listening to new stories. She needs about three or four months. Since both the children studied in boarding schools, they don't know Malayalam very well. Appu knows it better, though.You can understand that if you watch his first movie. Jeethu didn't give him many dialogues in 'Aadhi'. But because he has done so many movies now and has spoken to everyone on the sets, his Malayalam has improved considerably.Why Vismaya Mohanlal's Malayalam is limitedSuchitra Mohanlal explained that Vismaya Mohanlal entered boarding school much earlier than her brother. Pranav Mohanlal reportedly joined one when he was in sixth grade. Vismaya Mohanlal went to one while she was still in third grade.âMaaya has that particular problem. Appu went to boarding school when he was in sixth grade. Maaya went when she was in third grade. Most of the children studying there were foreigners. They mostly spoke English. Even when they came home, I spoke to them in English. That is my fault.English was also spoken in Suchitra's familySuchitra Mohanlal said English was not unusual in her own family either. She explained, âWhen I was growing up, we siblings also spoke in English to some extent. That's because Daddy speaks half Tamil and half Malayalam. Mummy is completely Malayali. We speak Malayalam with Mummy. With Daddy, we speak all three, that are English, Tamil and Malayalam.âShe also explained that Mohanlal's busy shooting schedule meant he was frequently away from home. As a result, the children had fewer opportunities to regularly communicate with him.Vismaya Mohanlal lacks confidence in MalayalamSuchitra Mohanlal said the family circumstances gradually reduced her children's connection with Malayalam.âThen when the children came along, their uncle (Mohanlal) wasn't at home either. He was mostly away shooting. I would speak to them over the phone when they were at the hostel every week. When they came home, their cousins had also been born and brought up in Madras, so they too spoke in English."She added, âSo, as they grew up, they lost their connection with Malayalam. When they come here, they speak to their father and mother. Other than that, they don't really have any other connections. Maaya can speak Malayalam, but she doesn't have the confidence to speak it. Then there is the slang. Everyone says I myself have a Tamil influence in my speech.âVismaya Mohanlal needs time for movie projectsSuchitra Mohanlal also explained why Vismaya Mohanlal may take longer before taking up a movie. She said, âMaaya reads scripts in English. She says she needs a month to learn the dialogues. That's why it won't happen immediately. Even if a good project comes along, she needs about a month or a month and a half.âVismaya Mohanlal recently made her acting debut with the movie 'Thudakkam'. In the same interview, Suchitra also revealed that her son Pranav has committed to a project, but she doesn't know the details.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Humanoid robots smash Usain Bolt’s 100-meter record
articles.summary: ﻿Literally ‘smashing’ — the bots can’t stop without colliding into a crash pad.
articles.body: The 9.58-second 100-meter dash record set by Usain Bolt in 2009 has been outpaced by Chinese robots participating at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing. In a preliminary heat on Saturday, Tiangong Ultra, made by the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation ​Center, ran the distance in 9.39 seconds, followed by the Honor-developed Lightning at 9.47 seconds. It’s one of several notable achievements to take place at the event, which can best be described as a sort of annual robot olympics that’s designed to showcase advancements in bipedal bot technology. After launching in 2025, 2,056 robots from 16 countries are participating in this year’s World Humanoid Robot Games, which includes categories for sprinting, jumping, football, boxing, and more. Tiangong Ultra also ran the 400-meter race in 38.16 seconds — beating the 43.03 second world record set by Wayde van Niekerk in 2016. [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zbkqhor3EKI] Unlike human athletes, however, these sprinting bots don’t typically get to perform a victory lap after crossing the finish line. Several videos show the robots colliding into cushioned walls at impressive speeds, where they (or the pieces of what’s left of them) get collected and carried away on a stretcher. Watching the various robot models actually run is both amusing and a little unsettling, given the bizarre way they move to dash so quickly.

articles.title: Motown songwriter behind 'Money (That's What I Want)' and other hits dead at 87
articles.summary: Janie Bradford Hobbs co-wrote "Money (That's What I Want)" with Berry Gordy and penned hits for Marvin Gaye, Stevie Wonder and The Supremes.
articles.body: Janie Bradford Hobbs, an early Motown songwriter who co-wrote "Money (That’s What I Want)" and penned songs recorded by Marvin Gaye, Stevie Wonder and other music legends, has died after an extended illness at 87. Bradford Hobbs died at a Los Angeles hospital, her family said Saturday. Born in Charleston, Missouri, Bradford Hobbs later moved to Detroit, where neighbor and singer Jackie Wilson introduced her to Motown founder Berry Gordy in the late 1950s. COMMODORES CO-FOUNDER AND FORMER BASSIST RONALD LAPREAD DEAD AT 75 She started working for Motown as a receptionist in 1958, but her role soon went well beyond answering phones. Like many employees in Motown’s early days, Bradford Hobbs became involved in making the music. She and Gordy wrote "Money (That’s What I Want)," which Barrett Strong recorded in 1959. The song became one of Motown’s first hits and was later recorded by The Beatles. Bradford Hobbs also wrote "Too Busy Thinking About My Baby." The Temptations recorded the song first, and Marvin Gaye later had a hit with it. She also wrote songs for Stevie Wonder, The Supremes, Martha & The Vandellas and others. "Janie was there with me from the very beginning, before there was even a Motown, and she will always hold a very special place in my heart and in the Motown family," Gordy said in a statement. COUNTRY MUSIC ICON DON SCHLITZ, WHO WROTE KENNY ROGERS' HIT 'THE GAMBLER,' DEAD AT 73 Gordy described Bradford Hobbs as one of the people who believed in Motown before anyone knew what it would become. "Janie was one of a special group I have always thought of as the original Motown family — the unsung heroes who believed in the dream before anyone knew what Motown would become," Gordy continued. "She was one of the people who helped make Motown what it became." Bradford Hobbs later became head of Writer Relations for Jobete, Motown’s publishing company. After leaving Motown, she founded the annual Heroes and Legends Awards, which honored figures in the music industry and awarded scholarships for about 30 years, according to her family. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP She is survived by her husband, Wardean Hobbs; daughter, Nicole Hobbs; son, Lance Finney; and two grandsons. Funeral arrangements have not been completed. articles.title: John Candy's family calls out Hollywood for weight criticism the actor endured throughout his career
articles.summary: Jennifer Candy-Sullivan and Rosemary Candy slam Hollywood's weight criticism of John Candy, revealing how the late comedian handled it privately.

articles.title: Hayden Panettiere's mom disputes her daughter's claim about their painful split: 'I didn't say what she said'
articles.summary: Lesley Vogel opened up about their estrangement and her concerns about Panettiere's on-and-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson.
articles.body:
Hayden Panettiere 's estranged mother, Lesley Vogel, has disputed the late actor's account of the moment she said she wanted to end their professional relationship, denying that she told her daughter, "You owe me."

In her memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning , which was published in May, Panettiere said that while filming the TV show Heroes at 19, she told Vogel she no longer wanted her to be her manager.

"I said to her, 'I don't want us to work together anymore. I just want you to be my mom,'" Panettiere recalled. According to Panettiere, Vogel responded, "You owe me."

The actor said she "remembered" feeling hopeful about the conversation, but said it was "disappointing" when she came to believe her mother was referring to money. "The fact that she didn't care to have a relationship with me was a tough pill to swallow," she added.

Panettiere died on Aug. 16 at 36. Her cause of death has yet to be confirmed.

In a new interview with ABC News , Vogel said she recalled the conversation taking place in Panettiere's trailer, but denied saying the words attributed to her.

"I remember being in her trailer and literally saying nothing," she said. "I knew that day would come — it's not that I didn't expect it — but it was very short, [a] very brief conversation, and then she turned and went to set… I know I didn't say what she said."

Panettiere's death has raised questions about how child stars in the entertainment industry are treated, with Anna Paquin among those who have called for greater protection for young actors.

Panettiere was 11 months old when she first appeared onscreen in a Playskool commercial. She went on to star in numerous TV shows and films — including Heroes , Nashville and two Scream movies — but struggled with drug addiction, postpartum depression and an abusive relationship with her on-and-off boyfriend, Brian Hickerson.

Here are the key points that have emerged since Panettiere died.

What was her relationship with her mom, Lesley Vogel?

Panettiere was estranged from her mother, who helped launch her career as a child model and later oversaw her work as a child actor.

In her memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning , Panettiere described Vogel as a "perfectionist" and recalled feeling pressure to succeed from a young age. She alleged that her mother would become angry when she failed to land roles and once superglued a fallen tooth back into her mouth because she feared it could cost Panettiere a job.

Vogel has disputed Panettiere's characterization of her childhood, telling the Daily Mail that she was demanding but did not force her daughter to work or abuse her. "I was strong, definitely, but I was not abusive by any stretch of the imagination," she said.

Vogel said their relationship remained close through much of Panettiere's childhood and adolescence but began to change when her daughter was around 16 or 17. Vogel attributed their later estrangement in part to her attempts to intervene in Panettiere's relationship with her boyfriend, Brian Hickerson.

"I had to go no contact because I could not help her anymore. I could not change this pattern, and believe me, I tried," Vogel said. "I didn't leave because I didn't care about her or didn't love her. I put so much effort in trying to save her. You cannot save someone who doesn't want to be saved."

What was her relationship with her boyfriend, Brian Hickerson?

Panettiere and Hickerson had a turbulent on-and-off relationship that included documented domestic violence. In 2021, Hickerson pleaded no contest to two felony counts of injuring Panettiere and was sentenced to 45 days in jail , probation and domestic violence classes. Hickerson later told TMZ , "I had a lot to drink, and I got physical with her."

Panettiere addressed the allegations publicly in 2020, saying she hoped sharing her experience would "empower others in abusive relationships to get the help they need and deserve." She also said she was "prepared to do my part to make sure this man never hurts anyone again."

In her memoir, Panettiere wrote about her decision to "let go of my resentment" and try to forgive Hickerson. She added, "I needed him to admit his wrongs and change because of them, but I didn't want to traumatize him in an irreversible way."

Months before her death, Panettiere had reportedly taken steps to keep Hickerson away. The New York Times reported, citing two people with direct knowledge, that private security accompanying her book tour in May had instructions not to let Hickerson into events.

"I needed an incredible amount of support and backup in order to make sure that there was no way for him to find his way back in," Panettiere told the podcast On Purpose .

Vogel described her daughter's relationship with Hickerson as codependent, saying, "When Brian came into her life, the changes started to occur. Very early in the game, I thought he's a modern-day gigolo. I know what he's after.

"I would talk to both of them about it. I would say, 'This is a codependent relationship, and it is not healthy for either of you. My sadness is that everything that I did, her father did, friends did, business people did, we could not break that codependent bond. It is so much more powerful than people understand."

Vogel told ABC News, "She knew that Brian was toxic. She knew she had to get him out of her life."

Hickerson has not been accused of a crime in connection with Panettiere's death.

Hickerson addressed Panettiere's death through his attorney, Sloan Ellis, saying, "Hayden's death remains under investigation, and it is important to allow that investigation to proceed.

"As has been publicly reported, police confirmed there were no signs of foul play. Out of respect for Hayden's loved ones and the ongoing investigation, there will be no further comment at this time."

What was her relationship with the father of her child, Wladimir Klitschko?

Panettiere dated boxer Wladimir Klitschko on and off between 2009 and 2018. They got engaged in 2013 , but never married, and their daughter, Kaya, was born in 2014. Panettiere was open about her struggles with alcohol and depression, including postpartum depression after Kaya's birth.

Kaya, who is 11, lives with Klitschko in Ukraine. Panettiere told the On Purpose podcast, "I think there's been this very common misconception that I just gave up my child. That could not be farther from the truth."

Panettiere said Klitschko suggested their daughter live with him full-time when Kaya was 2. She said she was in a "horrible cycle for years of battling depression and anxiety and alcoholism and substance abuse."

In a statement shared to Instagram after Panettiere's death, Klitschko wrote, "The announcement of Hayden's tragic death saddens me deeply. She left this world far too soon. Hayden was, although no longer my partner, an important part of my life and the mother of our daughter, Kaya."

Why has there been backlash against Neutrogena?

Panettiere was a longtime spokesperson for Neutrogena , appearing in commercials for the skin care brand for more than a decade. She alleged that the company wanted to end their relationship after she spoke publicly about experiencing postpartum depression in 2015.

"Of all the things… that they would fire me over, this was the last thing I thought they would fire me over," Panettiere told On Purpose.

Panettiere said her representative intervened and she was not immediately dropped, but that her relationship with the company subsequently ended.

"I'd worked with these people for 10 years, and I remember not hearing a word from anybody, not a 'great working with you for 10 years,' 'hope you're good; we wish you well.' And I remember that really breaking my heart."

Her allegations drew criticism of Neutrogena when they became public in May and resurfaced following her death, with some social media users calling for a boycott of the brand.

"For more than a decade, Hayden was a valued member of our Neutrogena community," Neutrogena said after her death. "We are proud to have partnered with her and understand that we made her feel unsupported during a very difficult time. This is not what Neutrogena stands for or who we want to be."

What else did she say in her recent memoir?

Panettiere released her memoir in May, three months before her death. The book traced her life from child stardom through some of her most difficult years, including her struggles with addiction and the death of her younger brother, Jansen, in 2023.

She wrote about how closely her own life began to mirror that of her Nashville character, Juliette Barnes, whose storylines included postpartum depression and problems with alcohol and pills. At the time, Panettiere was dealing with anxiety and addiction herself, writing that she eventually reached a point where she "needed a drink to function."

"Every time I read the day's script, it was like I was looking in a funhouse mirror, seeing a distorted reflection of myself. I can't tell you how lost this made me feel," she wrote.

Panettiere described herself as a "work in progress" in the memoir. In its closing pages, she wrote, "I just keep swimming, and with each stroke, I get stronger. With each passing day, I get to laugh a little more, learn another lesson, and make another friend."

What has been said about the cause of death?

Panettiere was found in cardiac arrest after emergency responders were called to the Greenville, S.C., residence where she was temporarily staying, according to the Greenville County Coroner's Office. She was pronounced dead after attempts to resuscitate her were unsuccessful.

An autopsy found no signs of trauma that contributed to her death, the coroner's office said. Her cause and manner of death have not yet been determined and are pending additional testing.

articles.title: Stella Lefty has an inescapable hit song and a billionaire dad. Music's nepo baby boom is getting harder to ignore
articles.summary: Stella Lefty says she understands the chatter about her father's wealth. As more nepo babies climb the charts, that conversation is only getting louder.
articles.body:
Maybe you've heard it on the radio recently or come by it by way of your Spotify algorithm: A raspy pop-country song about taking a train back to Boston and a budding relationship, from an emerging artist who seemed to come out of nowhere earlier this year. Her name is Stella Lefty.

Her monthly listeners on Spotify nearly doubled to 15 million in May, when her breakout song "Boston" made the cover of the platform's Hot Country playlist. In addition to the single climbing the Hot 100, the 24-year-old Chicago native just nabbed two VMA nominations and released a new album, Long Way Home , on Aug. 21 — altogether a massive summer for someone who wasn't signed by a major label until earlier this year.

But there's a fact about Lefty that I can't stop thinking about every time I hear her song, which is often: She's the daughter of a billionaire.

Lefty's dad is Eric Lefkofsky, the founder of Groupon and Tempus AI. He's worth an estimated $4.8 billion, per Forbes , which makes him one of the 1,000 richest people in the world. Does that make her rise — and the rise of the many other nepo babies breaking out in music right now — any less exciting?

A scroll through the charts at the moment will yield you a list of artists with successful parents, varying from those who simply have some industry connections to those who are undeniable household names. There's Audrey Hobert, the star of NPR's latest Tiny Desk whose dad is a writer and producer known for Scrubs and The Middle ; Malcolm Todd, Hobert's brother who just scored a Gap ad and a VMA nod; Gracie Abrams, daughter of blockbuster writer-director JJ Abrams; and VMA nominee Magnus Ferrell , son of comedian Will Ferrell. Being related to someone well-connected in the industry is hot right now.

"If a family connection gets you a meeting, I can't call that a scandal. It's natural for a parent to open any door they can for their child. Most of us would do the same," Jay Siegan, a longtime music executive, tells Yahoo.

It's the most surefire way to skip past the pesky "unknown" phase of stardom and get access to resources that artists with day jobs don't have. But Siegan notes that "the door only stays open once. The audience is the great equalizer, and either someone resonates, or they don't."

The boom in stars with famous lineage isn't entirely new. What's different now, compared to the past when nepo artists like Ziggy Marley, Hank Williams Jr. and Rosanne Cash were developing their own careers with a boost from their parents' coattails, is just how much we're talking about it. Nepotism has become an obsession in the 2020s, in a world where people are constantly suspicious that there are unseen influences everywhere. It's hard not to resent the people who seem to have been born with a leg up in life .

Multiple music industry publicists tell Yahoo that it's best to be upfront about nepotism status from the beginning, because it'll inevitably become something the public fixates on. Maxwell James, who works in entertainment publicity, says he'd recommend "acknowledging the advantage without making it the center of the artist's identity."

No matter how hard you try to downplay it, audiences can tell when artists have benefitted from access, resources, relationships and early exposure, James explains. They'll need to prove themselves with their talent, showing that they belong at the upper echelon just as much as someone who's gifted but didn't get a head start.

In a recent interview with Vanity Fair, Lefty says it's obvious to her that there's going to be chatter about her father's wealth, "which I totally understand." "Me and my dad have spoken about this a lot since I even started music. He was like, 'The truth will set you free,'" she says. The interview didn't reveal any more of her thoughts on how her parentage affected her career, though.

There's really no denying that nepo babies have opportunities that other artists don't. For instance, Magnus Ferrell got an instant boost in fame when his dad played a snippet of his song on Michelle Obama's podcast this summer, though he wasn't necessarily an overnight success. Many of them also had parents rich enough that they never had to approach "starving artist" territory. Not needing a day job while you plug away at your craft is a massive luxury.

James says the worst thing a nepo baby can do is appear defensive about whether they "deserve" their success. Gracie Abrams was praised for acknowledging in an interview with the New York Times' Popcast that she has "privilege" and a "safety net" afforded to her by her parents' status in Hollywood — and their wealth. "That allowed me the ability to experiment and to concentrate and I had the gift of time to dedicate to doing this thing I loved. I wasn't growing up afraid financially, and that's the biggest deal," she says.

That may elide, nevertheless, what really matters: connections. Those contacts could be vaguely in entertainment, where a meeting can go a long way, or it could be specifically within the opaque music industry. There's a difference between Billie Eilish's parents , who were working actors, and Clairo's dad, who was a high-level marketing exec with label connections. That sparked debate about which artists might be industry plants , a common concern among music fans worried that an up-and-coming star might be "planted" on the charts by record labels, rendering them inauthentic and unworthy of their success.

Nepotism doesn't guarantee success, of course. Plenty of celebrity and industry children try and fail, while random singers take off on TikTok all the time. Though let's be honest — any breakout success on an algorithm-driven platform, be it a streaming service or a social media site, can always have paid promotion behind it. As I type this, there's a massive ad for Lefty's album dominating my Spotify homepage.

Nickie Robinson, a music marketer, notes that a lot of these nepo babies honed their talent in the first place because they could afford tutoring and lessons from a young age. She sees it as a gift, but one that should be acknowledged by the beneficiary.

"Remember, labels only care about numbers, and most nepo babies have a substantial following from their parents and associated proximity bias. Why not leverage it?" she says, admitting they sometimes get on her nerves when she notices how plainly their parents can open doors for them. But, just like everyone else, they have the option to ignore the haters and just keep working.

"In this industry, you cannot care what people think. They will always have something to say, regardless," she says. Might as well let them.

articles.title: Meghan Markle's rumored return to acting in Netflix's 'The Gentlemen' draws conflicting reports
articles.summary: Reports link the Duchess of Sussex to Guy Ritchie's "The Gentlemen." She hasn't taken a scripted role since leaving "Suits" in 2018.
articles.body:
Meghan Markle's reported return to acting continues to generate speculation, with conflicting accounts as to whether the Duchess of Sussex is being lined up to star in Guy Ritchie's Netflix crime drama The Gentlemen following her U.K. move .

Deadline first reported on the rumors that Meghan could join the show's cast last week but cautioned that talks were hypothetical, in part because Netflix had yet to officially renew The Gentlemen beyond its second season, which premieres Sept. 3.

On Monday, while releasing the trailer for the show's second season, the streaming giant confirmed that Season 3 is coming, with Ritchie back to direct. In a statement, Ritchie wrote: "A third season felt inevitable, and I'm looking forward to pushing the boundaries of it further."

No mention of Meghan was made, however, leaving a lingering question mark hanging over any potential role she may play in the show.

On Saturday, Tina Brown, the former editor-in-chief of Vanity Fair and The New Yorker, reported that the offer had been withdrawn, citing a backlash in the U.K. Brown, a prominent journalist who is widely regarded as an expert on the royals, wrote in a Substack column: "I learned this morning that the casting of Meghan Markle in season 3 of Guy Ritchie's Netflix series The Gentlemen has been withdrawn. The backlash in the UK was so intense, it became untenable to go forward. This does not bode well for Meghan's acting comeback in the UK."

However, U.K. newspaper The Sun reported on Sunday that Meghan remained in talks to star in the show, citing an unnamed source as stating "no formal agreement has been reached." An additional account reported by The Times of London on Sunday suggested that Netflix executives had been unaware of any preliminary offer.

Sources close to the Sussexes have not denied that Meghan was offered a role, the BBC reported. Bronte Coy, the news.com.au reporter who first reported it, told BBC Radio 4 the project is a "top secret" U.K. production and that it played a "significant" part in the family's decision to return.

Meghan, her husband Prince Harry and their two young children are reportedly moving back to the U.K. this month , ahead of their children starting school in Britain in September. The Associated Press reported that they have already been enrolled, citing a person close to the Sussexes who was not authorized to speak publicly.

According to ABC News , the couple hasn't decided how long they will stay in the U.K. They plan to remain for an "extended period of time," according to a source familiar with the matter.

Apart from a recent cameo as herself in the Amazon MGM Studios movie Close Personal Friends , which stars Lily Collins and Brie Larson and is currently in post-production, Meghan's acting career has been on hold since her last episode of Suits aired in 2018. She played paralegal Rachel Zane in the USA Network legal drama for seven seasons.

Much of Meghan's recent television work has centered on the Netflix lifestyle series With Love, Meghan , which she hosted and executive-produced. The 2025 series grew out of Meghan and Harry's wider relationship with Netflix. In September 2020, eight months after stepping back from their duties as senior royals, the couple signed a deal with the streaming service through what would become their production company, Archewell Productions. The deal was widely reported to be worth around $100 million.

Their Netflix projects have included the six-part 2022 documentary series Harry & Meghan , Live to Lead (2022), a docuseries profiling prominent activists and leaders; Heart of Invictus (2023), which followed competitors preparing for the Invictus Games; and Polo (2024), a five-part series about players competing in the U.S. Open Polo Championship.

In August 2025, Netflix announced that Archewell Productions had signed a new multiyear first-look deal covering its film and television projects. The terms were not disclosed. Their new output included the second season of With Love, Meghan and a holiday special in December 2025.

Alongside her potential return to acting, the BBC reported that Meghan hopes to expand the global reach of her U.S.-based lifestyle and cooking brand, As Ever, after returning to the U.K. A partnership between the brand and Netflix helped launch it, but the streaming giant stepped down as a backer in March. "As it was always intended, Meghan will continue growing the brand and take it into its next chapter independently," a Netflix spokesperson told Variety at the time.

Upon their reported return to the U.K., the Sussexes are expected to settle in a privately owned home outside London rather than a royal property, according to the Associated Press. They also intend to keep their Montecito, Calif., home and a vacation property in Portugal. Harry and Meghan do not plan to resume their roles as working members of the royal family.

The Daily Telegraph was the first outlet to report the plans. People magazine subsequently reported on the relocation, while Reuters said a source close to Harry and Meghan had confirmed the plans.

Neither a spokesperson for Harry and Meghan nor Buckingham Palace has publicly confirmed the move. Harry said he had "nothing to say" when asked about the reports Wednesday night during an event with U.S. veterans in Washington.

The reported move comes as Harry has sought to repair his relationship with his family, particularly his father, King Charles III.

articles.title: Melissa Gilbert pleads to protect child actors after Hayden Panettiere's death at 36
articles.summary: Melissa Gilbert named three female child actors who died within one year as she demanded real substantive change for young performers.
articles.body: Melissa Gilbert made a passionate plea for child actors in the wake of Hayden Panettiere's death. Gilbert, 62, admitted that she didn't personally know the "Heroes" actress, but took Panettiere's death personally as she begged for industry changes in a post shared on Substack. "Within one year, Michelle Trachtenberg, Daveigh Chase and Hayden Panettiere have died," Gilbert wrote. "Three former female child actors of the same generation are gone. Tragically, heartbreakingly, agonizingly too soon." HAYDEN PANETTIERE'S CO-STAR JUSTIN CHATWIN 'P----- OFF' OVER HOLLYWOOD CULTURE AFTER HER PASSING "They are gone and the question I have been turning over and over in my head is, ‘WHY?". articles.title: Former child star Raquel Lee Bolleau alleges sexual assault on Disney Channel movie set
articles.summary: In a lawsuit filed last week, Bolleau claims Disney ignored signs she was being sexually abused while on set of the 2001 film “The Poof Point.”
articles.body: Former child actor Raquel Lee Bolleau alleges in a lawsuit filed last week that a male Disney employee sexually assaulted her while she was filming a network movie in 2001 and that the studio failed to respond to signs of abuse. Bolleau was 14 at the time of the alleged attacks, which she said unfolded during the filming of the Disney Channel movie “The Poof Point.” The plaintiff, now 39, said her alleged attacker, who is not named in the suit, was “a lifelong resident of California” who was more than twice as old as she was at the time. “John Doe” was “an on-set, adult, middle-aged, male employee of Disney who was involved in the filming of the movie” who “repeatedly raped, sexually assaulted, sexually abused and sexually harassed” Bolleau, according to the suit, which was filed in Los Angeles County Superior Court on Friday. “Mr. Doe’s sexual abuse of Ms. Bolleau was apparent to the adults on Disney’s set,” the suit states. “Disney repeatedly failed Ms. Bolleau.” A representative of Disney, based in Burbank, California, could not be immediately reached for comment Monday. Bolleau’s other credits include voicing Olei on Disney’s “The Proud Family: Louder and Prouder,” and Nubia Gross in “The Proud Family” original series and movie, according to IMDb. She has also appeared in shows like “Real Husbands of Hollywood” and films like “Stan the Man.” She alleges the abuse she experienced derailed her career because she had “trauma of returning to a set,” according to the lawsuit. Her lawsuit comes amid growing scrutiny of how child performers have been treated in Hollywood. The 2024 documentary “Quiet on Set: The Dark Side of Kids TV” detailed allegations of toxic working conditions on some Nickelodeon shows. Bolleau participated in the documentary, where she opened up about her experiences as a Black actor on “The Amanda Show,” but she did not discuss the allegations made in her recent lawsuit. Other former child stars have since spoken about the pressures of growing up in the industry and called for stronger support. Protections for child performers have expanded over the past decade, including new on-set advocates and tighter rules for adults working with minors. But industry sources told NBC News last week that safeguards remain inconsistent and have not kept pace with growing awareness of the potential mental health effects of child stardom. The alleged abuse toward Bolleau occurred in Utah, where “The Poof Point” was filmed, often in the man’s hotel room after he supplied her with alcohol, as well as on set, according to the lawsuit. “On set, Mr. Doe regularly fondled and excessively touched Ms. Bolleau, often rubbing his genitals on Ms. Bolleau while giving her unsolicited hugs,” the suit states. “No one from Disney stopped this extremely inappropriate touching and molestation of a child.” The abuse continued after the cast left Salt Lake City, with the man sexually assaulting Bolleau under a blanket as they flew back to California, the lawsuit said. Bolleau’s work on “The Poof Point” suffered due to the alcohol and sex, according to the lawsuit. “Disney recognized Ms. Bolleau’s sudden shift in demeanor and performance — clear indicia of child sexual abuse — and attacked, blamed and threatened Ms. Bolleau, a victim of rape, and Ms. Bolleau’s mother,” according to the lawsuit. The studio “has been protecting and empowering sexual predators,” the lawsuit adds. It’s unclear whether Bolleau or her guardian reported the 2001 assaults to the police. The suit does not mention any police involvement. Bolleau’s legal team declined to comment on whether law enforcement had ever been notified. Salt Lake City Police Detective Michael Ruff told NBC News in a statement Monday, “We do not have any records involving the name provided.” “There over a dozen police departments in Salt Lake County, without further details it’s difficult to know if the accusations occurred within our jurisdiction,” Ruff said. Bolleau’s lawsuit does not specify the amount of damages she is seeking. “Over the last decade, countless child actors have come forward to bravely share their experiences of abuse by adults in entertainment,” Bolleau’s attorneys, Douglas Wigdor and Jane Kim, said in a statement, adding that those responsible “directly or indirectly” should be held accountable.

articles.title: Kacey Musgraves divides fans with immigrant children’s plea, faces boycott calls to ‘shut up and sing’
articles.summary: Kacey Musgraves asked fans to donate to the Young Center for Immigrant Children's Rights during her tour opener, sparking a divided reaction on social media.
articles.body: Kacey Musgraves is facing backlash after asking fans to donate to an immigrant children’s rights group as her birthday wish while kicking off her "Middle of Nowhere" tour. On Friday, the country music star marked her 38th birthday on the opening night of her tour at the United Center in Chicago, Illinois. At one point, Musgraves paused her show and urged concertgoers to contribute to the Young Center for Immigrant Children's Rights. "It’s a wonderful organization, and they help give aid — legal aid — and money to children whose parents have been deported unfairly," Musgraves said. "It’s not a political thing. It’s just, these kids need help." She continued, "They have no guidance and no way to get through this thing without their homebase or their parents. So anyway, 50 cents, whatever the hell, I don't know, whatever you want to do but that would mean a lot to me." KACEY MUSGRAVES FACES BOYCOTT CALLS AFTER ASKING FANS TO DONATE TO IMMIGRANT CHILDREN'S GROUP "If you don't want to, that's totally fine too," Musgraves added. The eight-time Grammy Award winner's appeal was immediately met with applause and cheers from the crowd in Chicago. However, Musgraves' request drew a divided response online, including criticism from conservative political commentators. "What is an unfair deportation?" Tomi Lahren, host of Outkick's "Tomi Lahren Is Fearless" podcast, wrote on X alongside a video of Musgraves' birthday request. KENNY CHESNEY TELLS BILL MAHER THE KEY REASON HE REFUSES TO TELL HIS LISTENERS HOW TO VOTE "Kacey Musgraves stopped her concert to ask the audience to donate money for legal aid to kids whose parents have been deported ‘unfairly.’ How about donating money the help kids who's parents have been killed by illegal immigrants! What happened to the country music industry?" conservative influencer Vince Langman commented. "Another TRAITOROUS woman who wants nothing more than to see our country fall," an X user chimed in. "Shut up and sing Kasey (sic)!! Why do musicians think they Can draw a line in the sand? You alienate 50% of your audience," another commented. Some critics declared that they would no longer support Musgraves and called for a boycott of her music and concerts. NATALIE MAINES’ ANTI-TRUMP TIRADE, ZACH BRYAN’S FENCE-CLIMBING CLASH FUEL COUNTRY MUSIC’S BIGGEST FEUDS "You just earned yourself a big ol’ boycott, you traitor," one detractor wrote. "Illegal aliens and their kids don’t deserve our patronage and neither do you!" "I’m deporting Musgraves from all my music playlists," another X user commented. Other social media users argued that Musgraves should donate her own money rather than ask fans to contribute. "Kacey Musgraves is worth $15 million. Yet she’s asking fans who already paid $150 to $350 for tickets to donate to support the children of illegal aliens," one social media user commented. "If she cares that much, she can fund it herself and let them live in one of her multi-million-dollar mansions." MUSICIAN KENNY CHESNEY'S REFUSAL TO SPEAK OUT ON POLITICS SPARKS ARGUMENT ON 'THE VIEW' "Everyone she is speaking too (sic) gave her their money when they bought tickets," another added. "She did not give the audience money. So now she has the money, shouldn't she donate to whatever cause she wants? She is actually on stage at a show that the audience had to pay to get admission to and now she is asking for more of their money. That's rude." However, some of the "Dry Spell" singer's fans defended her on social media and praised her for speaking out on behalf of immigrant children. POP STAR OLIVIA RODRIGO FELT 'ENRAGED' AFTER ICE USED HER HIT SONG, BRANDS AGENCY 'BARBARIC' "Love this. 'It's not a political thing. It's just, these kids need help.' Exactly. More artists doing this please," one fan wrote on X. "In all fairness, the kids didn’t do anything wrong," another wrote. "I don’t believe their parents were wrongfully deported, but I equally believe that their children, if retained in the United States by law, should be taken care of. We’re not f------ animals!" "No boycott here!" an X user declared. "Helping children caught in difficult circumstances is a worthy cause," one commenter argued. "At the same time, immigration enforcement and whether a deportation was lawful or justified are matters for the courts and policymakers not concert stages." Fox News Digital has reached out to Musgraves' representatives for comment. Meanwhile, Musgraves stood by her remarks on social media, taking to her Instagram Story to upload a post that read, "Kinda chic when kids don't face immigration court alone." The singer also reposted a message shared by the Young Center's Instagram page, in which the organization expressed its gratitude to her. "Thank you," the nonprofit wrote. "We appreciate your support of our work and mission to see unaccompanied immigrant children safe, free, and with their families." Based in Chicago, the Young Center describes its work as pairing volunteers with attorneys and social workers to advocate for unaccompanied and separated immigrant children in government custody. Its website lists family unity, release from custody, fair proceedings and children's best interests among its priorities. The nonprofit reported serving 1,975 children from 53 countries in 2024 and opening 1,388 new cases. Its 2025 annual report said children's average detention time increased from 30 to 198 days and requests for assistance from detained parents quadrupled from 2024. Friday’s appeal extended Musgraves’ support for the charity. In April, resale platform Depop announced that 20 pieces from her wardrobe, including clothing from music videos and tours, would be sold in capsule drops. Women's Wear Daily reported that all proceeds would benefit the Young Center. In announcing the sale, Musgraves described the beneficiary without discussing immigration enforcement. "I also adore the fact that the sales are supporting a really beautiful cause," Musgraves said. Musgraves also invited three brothers, ages 18, 14 and 12, to open three Texas shows in May after their family was released from ICE custody. The mariachi performers' family said they entered through the now-defunct CBP One appointment system in 2023 and sought asylum after fleeing violence in Mexico, KSAT reported. "Unlike the previous administration, the Trump administration is not going to ignore the rule of law." Musgraves' latest remarks came as ICE enforcement reached record levels. articles.title: 'National Treasure' director predicts upcoming third film won't be able to 'ignore' politics
articles.summary: Director Jon Turteltaub said political polarization delayed "National Treasure 3" and explained the finished script will have to address modern politics.
articles.body: "National Treasure" director Jon Turteltaub suggested Friday that politics was a factor in delaying the third film in the Nicolas Cage-led franchise and predicted the issue would be addressed in the new sequel. During a live recording of the "National Treasure Hunt" podcast in Philadelphia, Turteltaub confirmed to an audience that "National Treasure 3" was "finally real" with a finished script approved by him and Disney. The original film, "National Treasure," came out in 2004 with its sequel, "National Treasure: Book of Secrets," premiering three years later in 2007. Both were directed by Turteltaub. 16 PATRIOTIC MOVIES TO WATCH THIS FOURTH OF JULY, FROM 'TOP GUN' TO 'SAVING PRIVATE RYAN' While discussing the gap between the second and third films, Turteltaub said that the growing political climate in the country made it difficult to keep working on the historical fiction film series, citing an interaction with former Republican House Speaker Kevin McCarthy. "He, like others, were surprised that Democrats made that movie because Democrats can’t be patriots," Turteltaub said, according to The Philadelphia Inquirer. "That’s the thought and it just got worse. And on the Democrats’ side: ‘Oh, Republicans, they just want to keep stuff to themselves, they hate everybody, they want to kill everyone, and blah blah blah.'" Though he did not offer many details about the third film, Turteltaub predicted that it would inevitably have to address modern politics. "We have to be very careful, but I don’t feel we are allowed to ignore it," Turteltaub said. "I think we have to include that idea in the story somehow without making someone feel put off." KELSEY GRAMMER ADMITS IT'S 'EXHAUSTING' WHEN MOVIES TRY TO ALTER HISTORY TO FIT MODERN TASTES Fox News Digital reached out to Disney for comment but did not immediately receive a response.  Turteltaub and producer Jerry Bruckheimer have hinted at the production of a third film starring Cage for years, though production has yet to take place. Even on the podcast, Turteltaub joked "things could happen" in the meantime. "Now, it’s Hollywood real, meaning things could happen. Nic gets hit by a bus, there’s no 'National Treasure 3.' If I get hit by a bus, there’s probably a 'National Treasure 3.' Welcome to Hollywood," Turteltaub said. In a comment to Fox News Digital, film critic Christian Toto, the founder and editor of Hollywood in Toto, said that it made sense for Hollywood to tackle another older franchise for nostalgia but expressed disappointment in the idea of addressing politics. DISNEY'S POLITICAL FIGHT WITH RON DESANTIS COST COMPANY YEARS OF THEME PARK EXPANSION, COURT RECORDS REVEAL "It sounds like Turteltaub, a veteran Hollywood director who isn't known for his political views, was accurately assessing how Hollywood views patriotism and the political divide," Toto said. "It's actually a sad sign of the times — a franchise about U.S. history is now seen as problematic or challenging, when it should be nothing of the kind." "Heck, if that delicate balance works, it might be the biggest film in the franchise."

articles.summary: Paul McCartney, Jane Fonda e Mick Jagger prestam homenagens. Lenda da música country morreu nesta terça-feira, aos 80 anos.
articles.body:
Lenda da música country, a cantora e atriz Dolly Parton morreu nesta terça (25) , aos 80 anos. A informação foi confirmada pela família em um vídeo nas redes sociais.

Conhecida pela voz marcante, pelas perucas loiras e figurinos extravagantes, Dolly construiu um império no entretenimento a partir de suas origens humildes no estado americano do Tennessee.

Eleita para os Halls da Fama do Country e do Rock & Roll e vencedora de 10 prêmios Grammy, Parton expandiu sua atuação para além da música country, transitando pelo pop, bluegrass e pela era disco.

Artistas, colegas do gênero e outros famosas lamentaram a morte. Veja abaixo:

Dolly Parton se apresenta em Tóquio, em julho de 1979 — Foto: AP Photo/Tsugufumi Matsumoto, Arquivo

"Estou devastada. Acabei de saber que Dolly se foi. Sei que milhões estão de luto e quero dizer o seguinte: mais do que qualquer pessoa que já conheci, Dolly sempre estará conosco, porque ela era tão presente, tão poderosa, tão generosa e divertida que está entrelaçada em todas as nossas vidas e corações para sempre. Temos nossas memórias dela, suas músicas, Dollywood, "Como eliminar seu chefe", os milhões de livros que ela colocou nas mãos de crianças, todas as imagens icônicas que a trazem até nós. E tudo isso são bênçãos. Sejamos gratos por tudo o que ela nos deixou para aliviar nossa tristeza agora. Eu nunca conheci ninguém como ela. Ela era simultaneamente uma garota sulista travessa e divertida dos vales do Tennessee e uma pensadora profunda e sensível, capaz de enxergar as pessoas até o fundo de sua verdadeira essência. Ela era muitas coisas… letrista, cantora, multi-instrumentista, escritora, piadista, visionária, amiga leal, que nunca ia dormir antes de ela e suas amigas rirem tanto a ponto de precisarem cruzar as pernas.

Ela tinha o instinto de uma sobrevivente e parecia sempre saber exatamente o que fazer, exatamente o que dizer para consertar as coisas... e logo em seguida colocava a bunda para fora da janela do carro e mostrava o traseiro para a casa de Kenny Rogers. Ela era a personificação voluptuosa da empatia. Isso é algo dela que ela gostaria que todos nós levássemos conosco.

Aos seus fãs gays e trans, quero que saibam que ela amava vocês. Vocês sabem disso sem que eu precise dizer. Ela amava todos os seus fãs, e eles são uma legião. E vocês sabem que ela não iria querer ver vocês de luto agora. Vistam-se com estilo e celebrem seu espírito. Mas antes, assistam ao episódio final de 'Grace and Frankie', onde ela interpreta um Anjo, a chefe dos anjos da classe trabalhadora no Céu.

Descanse em paz, mulher linda. Nós te amamos."

"A magnífica estrela Dolly Parton morreu, e isso é muito triste. Ela era uma mulher maravilhosa. Eu a conheci em Nashville, no Grand Ole Opry, onde ela vinha se apresentando com o astro da música country Porter Wagoner e estava prestes a iniciar sua carreira solo. Ela era tão radiante e cheia de vida que é difícil assimilar a notícia de sua partida. Suas composições, seu canto e sua filantropia eram incomparáveis no mundo da música country, e é difícil imaginar viver em um mundo sem Dolly. Ela era uma mulher de negócios inteligentíssima, que entendia o valor de sua música e, o mais importante, o impacto que exercia sobre as pessoas em todo o mundo. Não houve honra maior para mim do que tê-la cantando minha música 'Let It Be' e, mesmo tendo feito apenas uma pequena contribuição nela, sinto-me muito honrado por ela ter feito isso. Tenho muito orgulho de tê-la conhecido e admiro seus talentos únicos. Obrigado, Dolly, pela linda música que você deu a mim e ao mundo inteiro. Nós sempre amaremos você, que Deus a abençoe e descanse em paz. Você foi a melhor."

Mick Jagger, vocalista dos Rolling Stones

"Que compositora e cantora incrível que Dolly era. Ela reuniu tantas pessoas. Vamos sentir muito a sua falta."

"Ah, Dolly. A única coisa que consegui dizer depois de nos encontrarmos pela primeira vez foi: 'ela realmente é um anjo caminhando na terra' e 'parece até que poderíamos ser irmãs'. Guardarei com carinho nossas risadas e conversas, e vou manter a sua sabedoria, sua visão bem-humorada da vida e seu senso de humor impecável no meu bolso para os dias difíceis. Nunca haverá outra igual a você, e quanta sorte todos nós tivemos de presenciar a sua magia singular, assim como sua voz, suas canções e seu coração únicos. A sua luz será algo que o mundo procurará para sempre para reencontrar. Eu sempre vou te amar."

"Dolly era um ser humano mágico e alegre. Ter a oportunidade de conhecê-la é um tesouro que guardo na minha vida. O sol brilha menos hoje."

"Sinto tanto ao saber da Dolly — ela era uma força da natureza. Que descanse em paz."

"Dizem para nunca conhecer seus heróis. Eles estavam errados sobre ela. "Certamente, sentirei falta de seu riso, suas piadas e seu ser. Descanse bem e em paz total, minha amiga. Meu coração está pesado."

"Nunca conheci a Dolly Parton, mas, meu Deus, como eu a amava. Acho que nenhum de nós precisava conhecê-la para amá-la. Uma das maiores que este país já produziu. Lenda. De verdade. Para sempre. "Dolly nos ensinou que você pode ser tudo e fazer tudo e a fazê-lo com gentileza. Que luz. Somos todos gratos por termos vividos na época de Dolly Parton. Sempre vamos amá-la."

"Dolly Parton tinha um jeito de fazer todo mundo se sentir especial, visto, acolhido e como se fossem velhos amigos. "Se realmente existem anjos na terra, acabamos de perder um. Dolly Parton. Nunca haverá outra igual. Eu a adorava com todo o meu coração e sempre guardarei com carinho o tempo que passamos juntos. Para sempre. Descanse em paz, linda Dolly."

"Chocado e devastado ao saber da morte de Dolly. Uma artista gigante — única e insubstituível, com o coração mais gentil."

"Sempre haverá só uma Dolly Parton. Que alma ela tinha."

articles.summary: Ela foi eleita para os Halls da Fama do Country e do Rock & Roll e ganhou 10 prêmios no Grammy. Informação foi revelada pelo sobrinho da cantora nas redes sociais.
articles.body:
Lenda da música country, a cantora e atriz Dolly Parton morreu nesta terça (25), aos 80 anos. A informação foi confirmada pela família em um vídeo nas redes sociais.

"Esse anúncio em vídeo é algo que Dolly me pediu há anos, antes que eu tivesse absorvido totalmente como uma realidade no futuro", disse Bryan Seaver, sobrinho e chefe da segurança da cantora.

"A tristeza fica conosco, não com a Dolly. Dolly viveu na luz e está nos braços de Jesus, com certeza, ao lado de Carl [Thomas Dean, seu marido, que morreu em 2025], seus pais e incontáveis outros que a assistiram e que queriam encontrá-la nos céus."

Em último vídeo nas redes sociais, Dolly Parton convidou para exposição sobre sua vida; veja

Relembre história de 'Jolene', clássico da cantora que ganhou versão de Beyoncé

"Dolly também abriu as portas para gerações de cantores, compositores, músicos e sonhadores de todos os campos da vida e de todos os continentes. Com seu exemplo, nós acreditamos que tudo era possível. Ela nunca viu uma porta que não pudesse abrir, e as portas que ela abriu fizeram e mudaram a história."

Dolly enfrentava problemas de saúde desde a morte do marido, Carl Dean, que morreu em março de 2025. Ela cancelou uma residência de shows em maio deste ano. Em entrevista à revista "People", publicada no dia 21, ela disse que "não prestou atenção [aos próprios problemas]" enquanto cuidava do marido.

"Mas ainda estou trabalhando e há muitas coisas que eu ainda quero conquistar", acrescentou.

Conhecida pela voz marcante, pelas perucas loiras e por seus figurinos extravagantes, Dolly construiu um império no entretenimento a partir de suas origens humildes no estado americano do Tennessee.

Com mais de 3 mil músicas em seu catálogo, a artista se consolidou como um ícone da cultura pop e expandiu sua atuação para além da música country, transitando pelo pop, bluegrass e pela era disco.

Sua trajetória na música e no cinema se tornou parte do cânone da cultura americana. Ao longo de sua carreira, Dolly compôs sucessos atemporais que se tornaram clássicos, regravados por artistas do calibre de Beyoncé e Tina Turner. São dela músicas como "Jolene", "9 to 5" e "Coat of Many Colors".

Também foi Dolly quem escreveu e lançou a balada romântica "I Will Always Love You", posteriormente gravada por Whitney Houston para o filme "O Guarda-Costas".

Dolly Parton durante evento em Nova York, em outubro de 2022 — Foto: AP Photo/Andres Kudacki, Arquivo

Nascida em 1946 em Sevier County, em uma cabana de apenas um cômodo às margens do rio Little Pigeon, Dolly era a quarta de 12 filhos de um agricultor sem terras. A família não tinha acesso a água encanada ou eletricidade, e o médico que atendeu seu parto foi pago com um saco de farinha de milho.

Foi no ambiente familiar, marcado por hinos e canções folclóricas ensinadas pela mãe, que ela aprendeu a tocar instrumentos como violão e banjo, fazendo suas primeiras apresentações no rádio ainda na infância e lançando seu primeiro compacto em 1959.

O primeiro grande avanço em sua carreira ocorreu em 1967, ao ser contratada para o programa de televisão do cantor Porter Wagoner. A parceria na TV rendeu diversos hits em dueto, mas a crescente popularidade solo de Dolly acabou superando a do parceiro.

Ao decidir deixar o programa para focar na carreira solo em 1974, ela compôs "I Will Always Love You" como uma homenagem de despedida. A faixa alcançou o topo da parada country duas vezes antes de se tornar um fenômeno pop na voz de Whitney Houston, em 1992.

Ao longo de mais de seis décadas de trajetória, a artista escreveu cerca de 3 mil músicas. Suas composições abordavam temas cotidianos com olhar empático e socialmente crítico, tratando da infância pobre em "Coat of Many Colors", da gravidez na adolescência em "Down From Dover" e do machismo no mercado de trabalho em "9 to 5", canção-tema do filme homônimo lançado em 1980 no qual ela também atuou ao lado de Jane Fonda e Lily Tomlin.

Lily Tomlin, Dolly Parton e Jane Fonda em '9 to 5' — Foto: Reprodução

Entre seus maiores sucessos nas paradas estão a colaboração com Kenny Rogers em "Islands in the Stream" (1983) e o aclamado projeto "Trio", gravado ao lado de Emmylou Harris e Linda Ronstadt. A artista também construiu um império empresarial no Tennessee com o parque temático Dollywood e investiu na indústria cinematográfica e na televisão.

Com 55 indicações ao Grammy e 10 vitórias, Parton também foi a terceira mulher mais indicada na história do Grammy, atrás apenas de Beyoncé e Taylor Swift.

Dolly não tinha medo de inovar ou experimentar em seu trabalho, o que a garantiu essa carreira tão versátil e duradoura.

“Eu não tinha medo de mudar. Eu esperava o sucesso, mas estava preparada para o fracasso. Não me importava se as pessoas achassem que eu estava errada. No fundo, eu sabia que estava fazendo a coisa certa", disse à Associated Press em 1979.

Eleita para os Halls da Fama do Country e do Rock & Roll, Dolly Parton também se destacou pela atuação filantrópica. Por meio da fundação Imagination Library, criada em 1995, ela distribuiu mais de 200 milhões de livros para crianças.

Defensora ativa da diversidade e da inclusão, a cantora aliou seu trabalho social a posicionamentos públicos acolhedores, tornando-se uma figura de apelo universal na música norte-americana.

Nas últimas décadas, conquistou novas gerações ao trabalhar com artistas como Miley Cyrus, de quem era madrinha, Sabrina Carpenter e Beyoncé.

Capa do álbum 'Flerte', de Xamã — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Duas semanas após ter cancelado, às vésperas da estreia, uma turnê que previa mais de 30 shows em 25 cidades do Brasil, Xamã se prepara para apresentar o quinto álbum de estúdio do artista, intitulado “Flerte” e programado para ser lançado na quinta-feira, 27 de agosto.

“Foram onze meses construindo esse universo com recortes de poesias escritas no bloco de notas, músicas regravadas, pessoas e texturas que fizeram esse desejo ganhar forma”, relatou o cantor e compositor carioca ao revelar a capa e a contracapa – esta com a tracklist – do álbum “Flerte”.

Além dos já conhecidos feats com Ludmilla (em “Moça”) e L7nnon (em “Tá de parabéns”), faixas lançadas em julho e em março, respectivamente, o álbum “Flerte” traz as músicas “Bagunçou minha sexta”, “Like a Michael”, “Meu sonho é tu”, “Chá de”, “Você tirou meu ar” e “A nova sagitariana”, totalizando oito faixas.

Três delas – “A nova sagitariana”, “Chá de” e “Você tirou meu ar”– trazem a rapper paulistana Amabii (artista que transita entre o rap e o R&B) e o rapper NP Vocal. O carioca Nomad se junta a Amabii e a NP Vocal em “Chá de”.

A produção musical do álbum “Flerte” foi orquestrada por Ramon Calixto, $amuka e Marcio Arantes.

articles.title: Inside Jaaved Jaaferiâs 7,000-sq-ft sea-facing Bandra home with Mediterranean design, earthy interiors, textured walls, family memories and breathtaking Arabian Sea views
articles.summary: For veteran actor and television personality Jaaved Jaaferi, home has always meant Bandra. The actor graciously recently opened the doors of his over .
articles.body: For veteran actor and television personality Jaaved Jaaferi, home has always meant Bandra. The actor graciously recently opened the doors of his over 7,000-square-foot sea-facing apartment, walking Architectural Digest through a thoughtful space that reflects both his personal history and his family's evolving lifestyle needs. Designed by Kush Bhayani of KULx Studio, the spacious home leans into a warm, Mediterranean aesthetic while weaving in decades of memories from Jaaved's life in the suburb.Jaaved Jafferi's return to Bandra, rooted in nostalgiaJaaved's move back to Bandra wasn't just about the address but was deeply personal. "I've been a Bandra boy all my life; I was here for 40 years," Jaaved shares, recalling how he split his childhood and early years between his first two homes in the suburb before eventually moving to Lokhandwala with his children.The decision to return was also influenced by his elder children, Meezaan and Alaviaa. While Jaaved once found Bandra's dense construction overwhelming, this particular apartment changed his mind instantly. His brief to designer Kush Bhayani was simple: minimal sophistication, described in three words â "Warm, natural, eclectic."The new residence consequently became a way of reconnecting with familiar surroundings while creating a contemporary family home.What does Jaaved Jafferi's home look like?Overlooking the Arabian Sea, the apartment is designed around earthy, sunbaked tones that give it an instantly calming quality. The living room is anchored by a sage-toned two-sided sofa, while plush, earth-toned furnishings and pops of green create a soothing, lived-in atmosphere. The interiors draw heavily from Mediterranean influences, with earthy shades and natural materials running throughout the apartment. The expansive living room features plush, earth-toned furnishings, complemented by green accents that give the space a calm and soothing character.Textured micro-concrete walls run through the entire home, a detail the whole family agrees on. Patterned rugs, cured wood logs and translucent stone surfaces add to the eclectic, rustic-meets-modern feel, while a cosy reading nook with a built-in bookshelf houses artefacts from the family's travels and an extensive DVD collection.The dining table and family spaces at Jaaved Jafferi's homeOne addition the family was especially keen on was a proper dining table, something increasingly rare in homes shaped by social media and OTT habits. Meezaan explains the shift it's brought about at home, noting that everyone now gathers to eat together instead of retreating to their rooms with their meals. The dining area features a sleek onyx slab table supported by wooden logs, paired with upholstered chairs, and lit by bespoke sculptural fabric pendant lamps.A long terrace serves as another favourite spot, where two generations of the family come together to talk and unwind. Alaviaa's room, meanwhile, stands out with rust-maroon and colourful accents against the home's earthy base, including a statement chair and a sinuous mirror.A reading nook filled with family memoriesThe apartment also makes space for Jaaved's love of nostalgia. A cosy reading corner incorporates a built-in bookshelf filled with artefacts collected during the family's travels, along with an extensive DVD collection. Objects bearing personal significance have been integrated into the interiors. The family's shared history is similarly reflected in Meezaan's collection of CDs, featuring artists such as Don McLean and Fleetwood Mac. The collection was gifted to him by his father.The terrace overlooking the Arabian SeaThe home's terrace provides perhaps its most striking setting. Stretching along the apartment, it offers the family an open space to unwind, converse and spend time together while looking out towards the Arabian Sea. For Jaaved, the terrace and the home as a whole represent a connection between different stages of his life, his childhood in Bandra, his years as a performer and his present life surrounded by his children.More about Jaaved Jaaferi's workOn the professional front, Jaaved Jaaferi has had a busy run through 2025 and 2026. He featured in the psychological thriller 'Mayasabha â The Hall of Illusion', directed by Rahi Anil Barve, which released in theatres on January 30, 2026. He also appeared in 'De De Pyaar De 2' and 'Inn Galiyon Mein'. Most recently, Jaaved returned to the comedy franchise that made him a household name with 'Dhamaal 4', reuniting with Ajay Devgn, Riteish Deshmukh, Arshad Warsi and Sanjay Mishra, which released around Eid 2026. He also has projects including 'Love & War' and 'Hera Pheri 3' in various stages of production.Give your child the gift of confidence! Claim your exclusive TOI Masterclass spot today!

articles.title: Raksha Bandhan 2026: Date, purnima tithi, shubh muhurat, Rakhi timings and puja vidhi
articles.summary: Trending News: Rakhi season is almost here. The Rakhis are out, sweet shops are getting busier and families are already making plans for that one special morning whe.
articles.body: Rakhi season is almost here. The Rakhis are out, sweet shops are getting busier and families are already making plans for that one special morning when brothers and sisters sit together for the ceremony.Raksha Bandhan will be celebrated on Friday, August 28, 2026. The festival, also known as Rakhi, falls on the full moon day, or Purnima Tithi, of the Hindu month of Shravana.If you're wondering when to tie the Rakhi, what the shubh muhurat is and what you need for the traditional puja, here's a simple guide.Raksha Bandhan 2026: Date and Purnima TithiAccording to Drik Panchang, Raksha Bandhan falls on August 28, 2026.The Purnima Tithi begins at 9:08 am on August 27 and ends at 9:48 am on August 28.There's a reason you may find slightly different Rakhi timings online. Hindu festival timings are worked out according to the local sunrise and other Panchang calculations, so the muhurat isn't necessarily identical in every city.Raksha Bandhan 2026: Shubh MuhuratFor New Delhi, the Rakhi-tying muhurat on August 28 is from 5:57 am to 9:48 am.That's a little over three and a half hours, giving families plenty of time to get together and perform the ceremony.The Bhadra period ends before sunrise in New Delhi on August 28, so it doesn't overlap with this Rakhi-tying window.If you're celebrating outside Delhi, though, check the Panchang for your own city before deciding on the timing.Raksha Bandhan 2026: Rakhi-Tying TimingsThe timing changes slightly depending on the city.In Mumbai, for instance, the Rakhi-tying muhurat is 6:22 am to 9:48 am on August 28, according to Drik Panchang.You might also see Choghadiya timings listed for the day. But those shouldn't automatically be taken as the Rakhi-tying muhurat. The two aren't necessarily the same.And if your family traditionally avoids Rahu Kaal for auspicious ceremonies, remember that this timing also depends on the city.Mumbai Raksha Bandhan 2026 TimingsRaksha Bandhan: Friday, August 28, 2026Rakhi-tying muhurat: 6:22 am to 9:48 amPurnima Tithi begins: August 27 at 9:08 amPurnima Tithi ends: August 28 at 9:48 amBhadra: Ends before sunrise on August 28These are Mumbai-specific timings. If you're celebrating somewhere else, use the Panchang for your city.Raksha Bandhan 2026: Puja VidhiThe actual Rakhi ceremony is pretty straightforward.After the morning bath and other daily rituals, the family can get the puja thali ready. Usually, it includes the Rakhi, roli or kumkum, akshat, a diya and some sweets.The brother sits down for the ceremony and the sister applies a tilak to his forehead, followed by akshat. She then performs the aarti and prays for his health, happiness and long life.Then comes the moment everyone is waiting for - she ties the Rakhi around his wrist and offers him sweets.The brother traditionally gives his sister a gift in return. And, depending on the family, there may be hugs, teasing, photographs and a lot of catching up afterwards.That's also why there isn't one rigid way to celebrate Raksha Bandhan. Customs can differ from family to family and region to region. Some keep the ceremony elaborate, while others prefer a quick puja followed by lunch together.At the heart of it, though, the idea remains the same: a day to celebrate the bond between siblings.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.standfirst: La cantante mexicana fue invitada de lujo a la presentación de la española
articles.summary: La cantante mexicana fue invitada de lujo a la presentación de la española
articles.body: La experiencia de los conciertos de la cantante española, Rosalía, no se remiten únicamente a vivir e interpretar con mucha pasión sus grandes éxitos, la realidad es que este es un espectáculo integral y una de las dinámicas que no solamente el público que asiste disfruta, sino que además de vuelve viral pronto en redes sociales es la del llamado ‘Confesionario’, en donde la también compositora invita a otra celebridad que saca a la luz un tema escabroso de su vida personal y en su primera presentación en la Ciudad de México, el turno fue para una colega suya, Kenia Os. La nacida en Mazatlán, Sinaloa, el 15 de julio de 1999 (27 años de edad), cuyo nombre real es Kenia Guadalupe Flores Osuna, ha literalmente encendido las redes sociales y es que ha hecho público una infidelidad de la que fue víctima hace algún tiempo, no sabemos cuándo y no sabemos exactamente a quién se refiere, pero si tenemos una gran e interesante especulación, pero primera, repasemos que fue lo que dijo y que tiene a todo el mundo atentos al chisme. “Ninguna de mis relaciones ha funcionado porque soy una mujer que pongo límites, digo lo que no me gusta y, bueno, todo este tipo de cosas que me hacen ser una mala mujer, obviamente, sabes”, dijo Kenia Os en el Palacio de los Deportes el pasado sábado por la noche. “Hoy vamos a hablar de un cacas”. “Yo estaba en un tour, yo iba a dejar el país por bastantes semanas, era un tour muy importante, mi tour por primera vez en Estados Unidos. Entonces, como buenas personas, cantantes que se están conociendo, nos prometimos paz, tranquilidad, armonía, nada de cosas turbias, lo típico”, aseveró durante el evento que corresponde al LUX Tour 2026. “De repente me doy cuenta que él etiqueta a una mujer, en oculto. ¿Cómo me di cuenta? Tengo muchas amigas y muchos gays. Obviamente le pregunté por qué etiquetarla en oculto, no me hablaste nada de ella. No me quiero ver loca, pero necesito un poquito mi espacio porque nos estamos conociendo, como buen hombre me dijo: ‘Nada que ver’, ‘estás loca, ni al caso’, ‘jamás andaría con ella’. Acto seguido, en ese tiempo que nos estábamos dando, tiempo muy corto, o sea, como 10 días, comienza a salir con ella”.

articles.title: Ester Expósito desvela por qué ya no hace escenas íntimas: "Hice suficientes en 'Élite"
articles.standfirst: La actriz explica que hay muchos proyectos en las que “hay escenas de sexo gratuitas”
articles.summary: Ester Expósito desvela por qué ya no hace escenas íntimas: "Hice suficientes en 'Élite"
articles.body: Ester Exposíto lleva años labrando una gran carrera como actriz. Una trayectoria que comenzó mucho antes de sus papeles en ‘Élite’. Su primera aparición en pantalla fue en la serie ‘Centro médico’. En la actualidad, ya es una de las actrices más reconocidas del panorama español. Tal y cómo explica en una conversación con Hugo Diego García organizada por GQ España, ese reconocimiento ha llevado a Ester a poder elegir o rechazar algunos proyectos por muchas razones, entre ellas, que considere que en el guion aparezcan ”muchas escenas de sexo gratuitas”. “Ya hice suficientes en ‘Élite’”, declara Expósito, “entiendo que era parte del producto, de cómo era, pero es verdad que luego decidí protegerme un poco más”. En la ficción juvenil de Netflix, los actores interpretaban a compañeros de instituto y se mostraban los comportamientos que se suelen tener en el ámbito privado a esa edad. “No hay nada de malo, porque al final en el cine o en la televisión retratamos la vida, y en la vida hay sexo, como también hay violencia”, explica la intérprete sobre la aparición de escenas íntimas en el cine. “No es que me niegue a tener escenas íntimas, pero sí que me niego a tenerlas cuando no son necesarias para contar la historia y son gratuitas o demasiadas”, concluye la actriz. Después Hugo le pregunta sobre cómo vive ella sus relaciones personales. “He tenido un proceso y un camino, porque yo creo un poco por la cosa que tenemos instaurada todavía del amor romántico y de que el amor duele”, comienza contestando Ester. “Mis relaciones siempre fueron un poco turbulentas. He tenido momentos felices, pero mis relaciones en el pasado siempre han sido muy intensas, muy dramáticas…”. Ahora, confiesa que ha madurado y que está en un momento muy feliz.

articles.body: Woody Allen has been a well-known figure in the entertainment industry for years. The star dabbled in everything, ranging from acting to directing and writing. Todayâs quote about learning how to be satisfied with life and what you already have comes from a place of experience for Allen.The quote of the day by Woody Allen reads, "The talent for being happy is appreciating and liking what you have, instead of what you donât have.âWhat did Woody Allen mean by this quote?This quote is directly from the filmmaker and actorâs book titled âWoody Allen on Woody Allen: In Conversation with Stig BjÃ¶rkman.â The quote essentially says that it is important to appreciate what you already have, rather than focusing on what you do not. While it is human nature to appreciate things you have not yet achieved more, it often results in people forgetting the things they once worked hard to achieve.He acknowledges that one should never stop striving for success and goals; however, the key to success is remembering where you came fromâyour roots. When happiness is attached to what you don't have, the finish line keeps moving. Obtaining the missing piece simply creates a new desire, leaving you forever dissatisfied with life.At the end of the day, focusing on existing relationships, current health, or present comforts and things you have anchors you in the moment. It transforms routine aspects of life into sources of genuine joy and helps you understand that you need a balance of wanting more, while also appreciating what you already have.About Woody Allenâs early lifeHeywood âWoodyâ Allen (born Allan Stewart Konigsberg) was born in Brooklyn, New York, on December 1, 1935. His mother worked as a bookkeeper, while his father was a waiter and also engraved jewelry. Woody had humble beginnings and was from a middle-class family. Over the years, the filmmaker and actor has been open about how his relationship with his parents was strained and that he did not connect well enough with them. As a child, he immersed himself in the arts to escape his turbulent childhood. This included reading comic books, listening to jazz radio, doing magic tricks, and playing the clarinet.From an early age, he was interested in filmmaking and studied the subject at NYU (from where he later dropped out after failing a class) and City College of New York. He also legally changed his name to Heywood Allen when he was 17 and started calling himself by the nickname, âWoody.âWoody Allenâs careerHe started in the industry writing for âThe Herb Shriner Show,' after which he also wrote for âThe Tonight Showâ and âCandid Camera.' He received his first Grammy nomination for his self-titled comedy album. He dabbled in Broadway, working on âDon't Drink the Waterâ and âPlay It Again, Sam.â He entered the film industry as a screenwriter with âWhat's New, Pussycat?â and the rest is history. Over the years, he has worked as a scriptwriter, filmmaker, director, and actor. His first time as a director came with âWhat's Up, Tiger Lily.'Over the course of his career in the entertainment industry, Allen has scored more than 75 writing credits, along with over 50 directing credits and 50 acting credits.Give your child the gift of confidence!
